top_signal.title: How to Use Scavenger Hunts to Onboard New Employees (Without the Awkward Icebreakers)
top_signal.summary: If you've ever watched a new hire sit stiffly through a PowerPoint on company culture, you know the problem: onboarding is often forgettable.   One thing that's worked surprisingly well for small teams is the  workplace scavenger hunt  — and not in a cheesy way. Here's a practical guide to making it actually useful.     Why It Works   New employees need to learn three things fast: 1. Where things are (physically and operationally) 2. Who the key people are 3. What the culture actually feels like day-to-day   A well-designed scavenger hunt forces all three naturally, without anyone having to say "let's go around the room and share a fun fact."     A Simple Framework    Step 1: Map your must-knows  List the 10–15 things every new hire needs to find or learn in week one. Think: where the supply room is, who handles invoicing, where to submit time-off requests, the WiFi password.    Step 2: Turn each into a clue or task  Instead of "find the supply room," make it:  "Find the place where we keep the thing that makes Mondays survivable (hint: it's not the coffee machine)."  Small effort, much more memorable.    Step 3: Add one people-based task per department  Require the new hire to find someone in each team and ask them one specific question — their favorite thing about working there, what tool they couldn't live without, etc. Instant warm introductions.    Step 4: Give it a time limit  60–90 minutes works well. Enough time to explore, not so long it
